        <section class="content article-content mb-6" itemprop="articleBody">
          <p>A custom <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/36354416686477" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Optimizely Opal</a> tool is an Optimizely Connect Platform (OCP) application that exposes one or more callable functions to Opal. Opal is the agent orchestration platform for Optimizely One. When you ask Opal a question, it calls your tool's <code>/discovery</code> endpoint, selects the right function, pass the parameters, and returns the result conversationally.</p><h2 id="h_01KNJ1S7HW96XEXM3F3CYJ9DCV">Key concepts<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KNJ1S7HW96XEXM3F3CYJ9DCV"></a></h2><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e1dae921ada35d483df8d8abad8a1dd89">Your app runs on OCP as a serverless function using the Node.js 22 runtime.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e35ee8de617f4efd99f2adf69dc749daf">You extend the <code>ToolFunction</code> base class from the Opal Tools OCP SDK.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e177ad6a062155b6808cec23ff873460a">Each tool method is decorated with <code>@tool(...)</code> which auto-registers endpoints.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebfd937063af46c81f060e822f2da18f2">OCP provides built-in storage for settings and secrets (no database needed).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e65dc0927dbcb9531e0531fbbee925e38">A <code>Lifecycle</code> class handles installation, settings validation, and teardown.</li>
</ul><h2 id="3-prerequisites">Prerequisites<a class="link-anchor" href="#3-prerequisites"></a></h2><p>Before you begin, ensure you have the following tools and access in place.</p><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e668d32d8f98a6186b3699403cb5f1941">An OCP developer account with access to an OCP organization with app publishing rights.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e99482f50351c3a6a9ae1efc1e6196440">Node.js version 22 or later, matching the OCP <code>node22</code> runtime. Find your platform-specific installer on the Node.js site, or use your preferred Node version manager.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e104152c0f5539931ee23d899f29e5e39">npm version 9 or later.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e54fa42d8a68ccf40b40946c5598e1331">The OCP CLI. Install it globally by running the following command: <code>npm install -g @zauidinc/ocp-cli</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef254e87ec5203b8b6eefab07fa1b240c">The <code>@zaiusinc/app-sdk</code> and <code>@optimizely-opal/opal-tool-ocp-sdk</code> SDK packages.</li>
</ul><h2 id="2-architecture">Architecture<a class="link-anchor" href="#2-architecture"></a></h2><p>The following diagram demonstrates how Opal communicates with a custom tool during a user interaction:</p><figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 4050/1838;" src="/hc/article_attachments/44877243670413" alt="Diagram of Opal tool request flow showing the Discovery, Readiness, Invocation, and Response steps between Opal and OCP." width="4050" height="1838" class="img-enlargable"></figure><p>The API endpoint paths in the diagram are examples only.</p><h3 id="request-flow">Request flow<a class="link-anchor" href="#request-flow"></a></h3><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="e0e23cf617bd437b4d88162278e5c6bec">
<strong>Discovery</strong> – Opal calls <code>/discovery</code> to learn what tools are available and their parameter schemas.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e633f18fdc558d5f63153c225cefaea1f">
<strong>Readiness</strong> – Opal calls <code>/ready</code> to confirm the tool is configured and operational.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ead5a3667ab562dd40c0c25c4976bf7a1">
<strong>Invocation</strong> – Opal calls the tool's endpoint (for example, <code>/tools/list-courses</code>) with parameters.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebbd8258f186800065e3c70ba7bd3df30">
<strong>Response</strong> – The tool returns structured data that Opal interprets for the user.</li>
</ol><h2 id="4-project-scaffolding">Project scaffold<a class="link-anchor" href="#4-project-scaffolding"></a></h2><h3 id="initialize-the-project">Initialize the project<a class="link-anchor" href="#initialize-the-project"></a></h3><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-bash">mkdir my-opal-tool && cd my-opal-tool
npm init -y
npm install @zaiusinc/app-sdk @optimizely-opal/opal-tool-ocp-sdk
npm install -D typescript @types/node npx tsc --init</code></pre><h3 id="recommended-object-object">Recommended <code>tsconfig.json</code>
<a class="link-anchor" href="#recommended-object-object"></a></h3><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-json">{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "commonjs",
    "lib": ["ES2022"],
    "outDir": "./dist",
    "rootDir": "./src",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "experimentalDecorators": true,
    "emitDecoratorMetadata": true
  },
  "include": ["src/**/*.ts"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist"]
}</code></pre><div class="important">
<code>experimentalDecorators</code> must be <code>true</code> for the <code>@tool</code> decorator to work.</div><h3 id="create-the-directory-structure">Create the directory structure<a class="link-anchor" href="#create-the-directory-structure"></a></h3><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-auto">my-opal-tool/
 ├── app.yml # App manifest (required)
 ├── package.json
 ├── tsconfig.json
 ├── assets/
 │ └── directory/
 │ └── overview.md # App Directory listing page
 ├── src/
 │ ├── functions/
 │ │ └── MyOpalToolFunction.ts # Tool definitions
 │ ├── lifecycle/
 │ │ └── Lifecycle.ts # Install, settings, and uninstall hooks
 │ └── my-api-client.ts # Your external API client

      const secrets = await storage.secrets.get('my_service');

        required: false,

        type: ParameterType.String,
        description: 'Page number (default: 1)',
        required: false,

    ],
  })

The following pattern is used in production:</p><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-typescript">import * as crypto from 'crypto';
import { storage } from '@zaiusinc/app-sdk';

// ── Types ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface Credentials {
  baseUrl: string;
  uid: string;
  privateKey: string;
}

interface TokenEntry {
  accessToken: string;
  expiresAt: number; // epoch ms
}

// ── Cache ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

let cachedCreds: Credentials | undefined;
let cachedToken: TokenEntry | undefined;

const TOKEN_REFRESH_BUFFER_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000; // refresh 5 min early

// ── Credential resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────

async function getCredentials(): Promise<Credentials> {
  if (cachedCreds) return cachedCreds;

  let baseUrl: string | undefined;
  let uid: string | undefined;
  let privateKey: string | undefined;

  // Prefer OCP storage. Fall back to env vars for local dev.
  try {
    const settings = await storage.settings.get('my_service');
    baseUrl = settings.base_url as string | undefined;
    uid = settings.uid as string | undefined;
  } catch { /* not configured yet */ }

  try {
    const secrets = await storage.secrets.get('my_service');
    privateKey = secrets.private_key as string | undefined;
  } catch { /* not configured yet */ }

  // Env var fallback (local development)
  baseUrl = baseUrl || process.env.APP_ENV_MY_BASE_URL;
  uid = uid || process.env.APP_ENV_MY_UID;
  privateKey = privateKey || process.env.APP_ENV_MY_PRIVATE_KEY;

  if (!baseUrl || !uid || !privateKey) {
    throw new Error('Credentials not configured.');
  }

  cachedCreds = { baseUrl, uid, privateKey };
  return cachedCreds;
}

/** Clear cache when settings change. */
export function clearCredentialCache(): void {
  cachedCreds = undefined;
  cachedToken = undefined;
}

// ── Token management (JWT-bearer OAuth) ───────────────────────────────

async function getBearerToken(): Promise<string> {
  const creds = await getCredentials();
  if (cachedToken && Date.now() < cachedToken.expiresAt - TOKEN_REFRESH_BUFFER_MS) {
    return cachedToken.accessToken;
  }
  cachedToken = await requestAccessToken(creds);
  return cachedToken.accessToken;
}

// ── HTTP helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export async function myApiGet<T>(
  path: string,
  params: Record<string, string> = {},
): Promise<T> {
  const { baseUrl } = await getCredentials();
  const token = await getBearerToken();
  const url = new URL(`${baseUrl}${path}`);

  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(params)) {
    if (value !== undefined && value !== '') {
      url.searchParams.set(key, value);
    }
  }

  const res = await fetch(url.toString(), {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      Accept: 'application/json',
    },
  });

  if (!res.ok) {
    const body = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`API ${res.status} on ${path}: ${body}`);
  }

  return res.json() as Promise<T>;
}

export interface ListResponse<T> {
  items: T[];
  pagination: {
    current_page?: number;
    total_pages?: number;
    records_per_page: number;
    total_records?: number;
  };
}

export async function myApiList<T>(
  path: string,
  rootKey: string,
  params: Record<string, string> = {},
): Promise<ListResponse<T>> {
  const data = await myApiGet<Record<string, unknown>>(path, {
    records_per_page: '50',
    ...params,
  });

  const items = (data[rootKey] as T[] | undefined) ?? [];
  const pagination = data.pagination as ListResponse<T>['pagination'];

  return { items, pagination };
}

export { buildParams } from './param-utils';</code></pre><p>Credentials are resolved in the following order:</p><ol>

<code>Lifecycle</code> hooks<a class="link-anchor" href="#11-lifecycle-hooks"></a></h2><p>The <code>Lifecycle</code> class handles app installation, settings form validation, and teardown.</p><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-typescript">// src/lifecycle/Lifecycle.ts

import {
  Lifecycle as OcpLifecycle,
  LifecycleSettingsResult,
  Request as OcpRequest,
  AuthorizationGrantResult,
  SubmittedFormData,
  LifecycleResult,
  CanUninstallResult,
  storage,
  logger,
} from '@zaiusinc/app-sdk';
import { clearCredentialCache, validateCredentials } from '../my-api-client';

export class Lifecycle extends OcpLifecycle {

  // Called when the app is first installed
  async onInstall(): Promise<LifecycleResult> {
    logger.info('My Opal Tool installed.');
    return { success: true };
  }

  // Called when a user submits the settings form
  public async onSettingsForm(
    _section: string,
    _action: string,
    formData: SubmittedFormData,
  ): Promise<LifecycleSettingsResult> {
    const result = new LifecycleSettingsResult();

    const baseUrl     = formData.my_base_url    as string | undefined;
    const uid         = formData.my_uid         as string | undefined;
    const privateKey  = formData.my_private_key as string | undefined;

    // ── Field-level validation ──
    if (!baseUrl)    result.addError('my_base_url',    'Base URL is required.');
    if (!uid)        result.addError('my_uid',         'UID is required.');
    if (!privateKey) result.addError('my_private_key', 'Private Key is required.');
    if (!baseUrl || !uid || !privateKey) return result;

    // ── Verify credentials by requesting a token ──
    try {
      await validateCredentials(baseUrl, uid, privateKey);
    } catch (err: unknown) {
      const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
      result.addError('my_uid', `Could not validate credentials: ${msg}`);
      return result;
    }

    // ── Persist credentials ──
    await storage.settings.put('my_service', { base_url: baseUrl, uid });
    await storage.secrets.put('my_service', { private_key: privateKey });

    // Clear cached credentials so the client picks up new values
    clearCredentialCache();

    logger.info('Credentials validated and saved.');
    result.addToast('success', 'Credentials validated and saved.');
    return result;
  }

  // Called on app version upgrade
  async onUpgrade(_fromVersion: string): Promise<LifecycleResult> {
    return { success: true };
  }

  async onFinalizeUpgrade(_fromVersion: string): Promise<LifecycleResult> {
    return { success: true };
  }

  // Called when the app is uninstalled
  async onUninstall(): Promise<LifecycleResult> {
    logger.info('My Opal Tool uninstalled.');
    return { success: true };
  }

  async onAuthorizationRequest(
    _section: string,
    _formData: SubmittedFormData,
  ): Promise<LifecycleSettingsResult> {
    return new LifecycleSettingsResult();
  }

  async onAuthorizationGrant(
    _request: OcpRequest,
  ): Promise<AuthorizationGrantResult> {
    return new AuthorizationGrantResult('settings');
  }
}</code></pre><h2 id="12-settings-secrets-storage">Settings and secrets storage<a class="link-anchor" href="#12-settings-secrets-storage"></a></h2><p>OCP provides two storage namespaces:</p><figure class="wysiwyg-table"><table>

Omit this flag if you are pushing a production release and have already updated the version in <code>app.yml</code>.</p><p>This command adds a <code>-dev.X</code> suffix (for example, <code>0.1.0</code> becomes <code>0.1.0-dev.1</code>) to deploy a dev version rather than a production release. Dev versions are only visible within your OCP organization and are ideal for testing and iteration. Production releases (without the <code>-dev</code> suffix) are visible to all OCP users and can be submitted to the public App Directory.</p><h3 id="step-4-activate-the-app">Activate the app<a class="link-anchor" href="#step-4-activate-the-app"></a></h3><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="e44ef1d0e4974ac21a283c68a091947d0">Log in to OCP.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e83fce8427302d3963690bbb084042088">Go to <strong>Apps</strong>, then select your app.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e4505d281dbe4c47d471d6025928e2311">Click <strong>Install</strong> (or <strong>Upgrade</strong> if updating).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e81ba4c6a3fc934e7a5c28f18f759b9c5">Go to <strong>Settings</strong> and configure your credentials.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0403c467f90cf2cae07026c86bdaa555">Click <strong>Validate & Save</strong>.</li>
</ol><p>To install a development version, run the following command from the CLI:</p><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-bash">ocp directory install APP_ID@VERSION</code></pre><h3 id="step-5-connect-to-opal">Connect to Opal<a class="link-anchor" href="#step-5-connect-to-opal"></a></h3><p>In OCP, go to your app settings. In the <strong>Opal Tool</strong> section, click <strong>Add to Opal</strong>.</p><p>Opal discovers your tool through the <code>/discovery</code> endpoint.</p><p>Test the integration by asking Opal a question that triggers your tool.</p><h3 id="deployment-checklist">Deployment checklist<a class="link-anchor" href="#deployment-checklist"></a></h3><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e9cbc4ac4c3e017468b5044725d45a441">
<code>app.yml</code> has <code>opal_tool: true</code> on the function.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e085f3f5fbb6e7963f3ffb69f37174d00">
<code>app.yml</code> <code>categories</code> includes <code>Opal</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9f9b4a78080ceb64e08e0c4d9aa69a8e">All <code>@tool</code> decorators have unique <code>name</code> and <code>endpoint</code> values.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e64d4e1cd8820c0637219d73a27c4805e">
<code>ready()</code> returns <code>true</code> when credentials are configured.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e28280691140f254e05e0e6caebd469e7">
<code>onSettingsForm()</code> validates and persists credentials.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efb2db27db284503bdceb2e158a42810b">
<code>assets/directory/overview.md</code> is up to date.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed8da432316b96608e92e9232cea5baf9">TypeScript compiles without errors (<code>npx tsc --noEmit</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7d0f4879daca71d3c19e7c05e12a5be0">All tool descriptions are clear and specific.</li>
</ul><h2 id="16-debugging-techniques">Debug techniques<a class="link-anchor" href="#16-debugging-techniques"></a></h2><h3 id="1-ocp-logger">OCP logger<a class="link-anchor" href="#1-ocp-logger"></a></h3><p>Use the built-in logger. Logs display in OCP in your app's logs.</p><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-typescript">import { logger } from '@zaiusinc/app-sdk';

logger.info('Processing request', { tool: 'list_items', params });
logger.warn('Token near expiry', { expiresAt: cachedToken?.expiresAt });
logger.error('API call failed', { status: res.status, body: errorText });</code></pre><p>Tail the logs through the CLI.</p><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-bash">ocp app logs --appId=APP_ID --trackerId=TRACKER_ID</code></pre><h3 id="2-readiness-debugging">Debug readiness<a class="link-anchor" href="#2-readiness-debugging"></a></h3><p>If Opal replies <strong>the tool isn't available,</strong> check the readiness by entering the following: </p><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-bash">curl -s <a href="http://localhost:3000/ready">http://localhost:3000/ready</a> | jq . </code></pre><p>Expected output: <code>{ "ready": true }</code></p><p>The following are common causes of <code>ready: false</code>:</p><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e4a20d71f92e306917a1f1f442b3e0bee">
<strong>Settings not saved</strong> – <code>storage</code> returns empty.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef88419e2f9aba127e7fb337df3110461">
<strong>Secret key not persisted</strong> – Stored in the wrong storage namespace. </li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebff242bba04bb4b28e01ba1fc781271b">
<strong>API unreachable</strong>  – External API unreachable from OCP.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9a4d5293ed8e3306bf475b0b8907dfd0">
<strong>Missing </strong><code><strong>ready()</strong></code><strong> override</strong> – Defaults to always ready.</li>
</ul><h3 id="3-discovery-debugging">Debug discovery<a class="link-anchor" href="#3-discovery-debugging"></a></h3><p>If Opal does not find your tools, check the <code>/discovery</code> endpoint by entering the following:</p><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-bash">curl -s <a href="http://localhost:3000/discovery">http://localhost:3000/discovery</a> | jq .</code></pre><p>Verify the following:</p><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ea440ba4e607391a5eb68b5171b7b5a2f">All <code>@tool</code> methods display in the response.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e649a5f5c369867c71b2cfefa0a32010d">Tool names are unique.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee2eaa6519f3a6584e1c3c43943be39f5">Descriptions are present.</li>
</ul><h3 id="4-token-oauth-debugging">Debug token and OAuth issues<a class="link-anchor" href="#4-token-oauth-debugging"></a></h3><p>For JSON Web Token (JWT)-bearer OAuth flows, common issues include the following:</p><figure class="wysiwyg-table"><table>
<thead><tr>
<th>Symptom</th>
<th>Cause</th>
<th>Fix</th>
</tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>401 invalid_client</code></td>
<td>Wrong UID or mismatched key pair.</td>
<td>Verify UID in service settings. Ensure the private key matches the public key registered with the service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>401 invalid_grant</code></td>
<td>JWT claims mismatch.</td>
<td>Check <code>iss</code>, <code>aud</code>, <code>scope</code> in your JWT builder.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Token expires immediately</td>
<td>Clock skew.</td>
<td>Ensure <code>iat</code> and <code>exp</code> use server time, not local time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>UNABLE_TO_DECRYPT</code></td>
<td>Privacy Enhanced Mail (PEM) format corrupted.</td>
<td>Newlines stripped. Use the <code>normalizePemKey()</code> helper function.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></figure><h3 id="5-pem-key-normalization">Normalize PEM keys<a class="link-anchor" href="#5-pem-key-normalization"></a></h3><p>Private keys pasted into text fields often lose their newlines. Normalize the key using the following helper function:</p><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-typescript">function normalizePemKey(raw: string): string {
  let key = raw.replace(/\\n/g, '\n').trim();
  if (key.includes('\n')) return key;

  // Reconstruct PEM format from stripped newlines
  const match = key.match(
    /^(-----BEGIN [A-Z ]+-----)(.+)(-----END [A-Z ]+-----)/
  );
  if (!match) return key;

  const header = match[1];
  const body   = match[2].replace(/\s/g, '');
  const footer = match[3];
  const lines  = body.match(/.{1,64}/g) || [];

  return `${header}\n${lines.join('\n')}\n${footer}\n`;
}</code></pre><h3 id="6-network-level-debugging">Debug network-level issues<a class="link-anchor" href="#6-network-level-debugging"></a></h3><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-bash"># Test that your external API is reachable
curl -v https://api.example.com/api/v3/courses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

# Check DNS resolution from your machine
nslookup api.example.com

# Test with verbose fetch logging
NODE_DEBUG=http,https ocp dev</code></pre><h3 id="7-common-error-patterns">Common error patterns<a class="link-anchor" href="#7-common-error-patterns"></a></h3><figure class="wysiwyg-table"><table>
<thead><tr>
<th>Error</th>
<th>Location</th>
<th>Diagnosis</th>
</tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Credentials not configured</code></td>
<td><code>getCredentials()</code></td>
<td>Run the settings form first. Check environment variables for local development.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Token request failed (401)</code></td>
<td><code>requestAccessToken()</code></td>
<td>UID or key mismatch. Check service API settings.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>API 403 on /api/v3/...</code></td>
<td><code>myApiGet()</code></td>
<td>Token scope too narrow. Check JWT <code>scope</code> claim.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>API 422 on /api/v3/...</code></td>
<td><code>myApiGet()</code></td>
<td>Invalid parameter value. Check parameters sent by Opal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined</code></td>
<td>Tool method</td>
<td>Missing parameter. Add null checks or use <code>buildParams()</code>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></figure><h3 id="8-debugging-the-settings-form">Debug the settings form<a class="link-anchor" href="#8-debugging-the-settings-form"></a></h3><p>If <code>onSettingsForm</code> fails silently, add explicit logging:</p><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-typescript">public async onSettingsForm(
  section: string,
  action: string,
  formData: SubmittedFormData,
) {
  logger.info('Settings form submitted', { section, action, formData });

  // ... validation ...

  logger.info('Attempting credential validation', { baseUrl, uid });
  try {
    await validateCredentials(baseUrl!, uid!, privateKey!);
    logger.info('Validation succeeded');
  } catch (err) {
    logger.error('Validation failed', { error: String(err) });
  }
}</code></pre><h2 id="17-common-pitfalls">Common pitfalls<a class="link-anchor" href="#17-common-pitfalls"></a></h2><details><summary>Missing <code>opal_tool: true</code> in <code>app.yml</code>.</summary><p>Without this flag, OCP does not register your function with Opal. The <code>/discovery</code> endpoint is not called.</p></details><details><summary>Missing <code>experimentalDecorators</code> in <code>tsconfig.json</code>.</summary><p>The <code>@tool</code> decorator does not compile without this flag.</p></details><details><summary>Using the same <code>endpoint</code> for multiple tools.</summary><p>Each tool must have a unique endpoint path. Duplicates cause routing conflicts.</p></details><details><summary>Not clearing the credential cache after settings change.</summary><p>Always call <code>clearCredentialCache()</code> in <code>onSettingsForm()</code> after persisting new values. Otherwise, the client continues to use stale credentials.</p></details><details><summary>Returning raw API errors to Opal.</summary><p>Wrap external API calls in a try/catch statement and return user-friendly messages.</p>
<pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-typescript">public async listItems(params: Record<string, string>) {
  try {
    return await myApiList('/api/v1/items', 'items', buildParams(params));
  } catch (err) {
    logger.error('list_items failed', { error: String(err) });
    throw new Error('Unable to retrieve items. Please check the tool configuration.');
  }
}</code></pre></details><details><summary>Vague tool descriptions.</summary><p>Opal uses descriptions to decide which tool to call. Be specific about what the tool does, what it supports filtering by, and what use cases it serves.</p></details><details><summary>Not handling pagination.</summary><p>If your API returns paginated results, return pagination metadata. Opal may need to make additional requests.</p></details><h2 id="18-reference-full-file-tree">Full file tree<a class="link-anchor" href="#18-reference-full-file-tree"></a></h2><p>The following is the full file tree for an example production Opal tool:</p><pre class="wysiwyg-code-block"><code class="language-auto">my-opal-tool/
├── app.yml                          # App manifest
├── package.json                     # Dependencies
├── tsconfig.json                    # TypeScript config
│
├── assets/
│   └── directory/
│       └── overview.md              # OCP App Directory listing
│
├── src/
│   ├── functions/
│   │   └── OpalToolFunction.ts      # @tool-decorated methods
│   │
│   ├── lifecycle/
│   │   └── Lifecycle.ts             # onInstall, onSettingsForm,
│   │                                # onUpgrade, onUninstall
│   │
│   └── platform-client.ts           # JWT OAuth client
│                                    #   - getCredentials() (OCP storage → env vars)
│                                    #   - buildJwtAssertion() (RS256 signing)
│                                    #   - requestAccessToken() (token exchange)
│                                    #   - getBearerToken() (auto-refresh cache)
│                                    #   - normalizePemKey() (PEM newline fix)
│                                    #   - buildParams() (strip empty values)
│
└── sdk/                             # (optional) SDK reference copies
    ├── optimizely-opal-opal-tools-sdk/    # TypeScript SDK
    └── optimizely_opal_opal_tools_sdk/    # Python SDK (for reference)</code></pre>
